title: Pushing the Limits of Inverse Lithography with Generative Reinforcement Learning
evidence_span: The framework treats a conditional Style-Aware GAN as a learned mask distribution and fine-tunes it with policy optimization plus imitation learning to avoid poor training-distribution and non-convex-refinement traps; the official description claims improved mask quality and reduced numerical-refinement time without numeric values.
problem: Inverse lithography is non-convex, and suboptimal training data plus expensive post-generation refinement can leave generative mask solutions in poor local minima.
method_or_artifact: Style-aware GAN pretraining on design data followed by policy-optimization and imitation-learning fine-tuning over mask distributions.
workload_or_benchmark: Inverse-lithography mask generation; design patterns, process node, lithography simulator, mask metrics, and refinement budget are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Semiconductor mask-generation and lithography simulation flow; optical model, process conditions, resolution, and manufacturing constraints are unspecified.
baselines: generative ILT methods with post-ILT refinement
limits: No mask-quality metric, process condition, pattern suite, runtime, or policy-training budget is supplied.
GAN distribution quality and manufacturability may depend strongly on training-pattern coverage.
Official description only; lithography fidelity and yield implications require paper-level verification.

title: Time-Aware Active Calibration and Scheduling for N-Qubit Systems via Bayesian Optimization and Reinforcement Learning
evidence_span: Cal Orchestrator models calibration parameters and dependencies as a DAG, represents drift with Ornstein–Uhlenbeck or exponential processes, selects experiments using Bayesian information gain per unit time, and schedules cross-qubit calibration with RL/ILP under online RB/XEB health triggers; the official description reports improved calibration efficiency and mean time between recalibrations versus fixed or heuristic scheduling, without numeric values.
problem: Frequent multi-qubit recalibration is costly while parameter drift reduces hardware fidelity and creates conflicts among calibration and readout tasks.
method_or_artifact: Dependency-aware calibration DAG, time-aware Bayesian experiment selection, RL/ILP cross-qubit scheduling, and self-triggered recalibration from RB/XEB health metrics.
workload_or_benchmark: Multi-qubit calibration testbeds with frequency, amplitude, DRAG, phase, and readout tasks; qubit count, drift traces, fidelity targets, and calibration budgets are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Superconducting or similar N-qubit control systems with time-varying parameters and online randomized-benchmarking/cross-entropy metrics; control electronics and timing are unspecified.
metrics: Longer mean time between recalibrations claimed qualitatively
limits: No qubit count, fidelity, drift timescale, calibration duration, or baseline values are supplied.
Information-gain and scheduling objectives may trade off fidelity, idle time, and experiment risk.
Official description only; open-source orchestrator and hardware/testbed claims require inspection.

title: HW-Router: Hardware-Aware Routing for Scalable Multi-LLM Serving
evidence_span: HW-Router predicts per-model/per-GPU latency from model features, input length, queue lengths, KV-cache utilization, and recent TTFT/TPOT, then makes SLO-aware routing decisions; across diverse workloads the official description reports 3.4–3.9x lower end-to-end latency, 46–48 percentage-point higher SLO attainment, 6–8x lower GPU-load skew, 3.1–3.4x lower queue fraction, and approximately 200 microseconds routing overhead versus CARROT and IRT.
problem: Static, hardware-agnostic multi-LLM routing misses GPU type, queue, KV-cache, and contention effects, causing SLO violations and load imbalance.
method_or_artifact: Real-time hardware-signal collection, lightweight per-model/per-GPU latency prediction, and SLO-aware multi-model routing.
workload_or_benchmark: Diverse multi-LLM serving workloads; model set, GPU mix, request distribution, SLO definitions, and warm-up/queue policies are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Heterogeneous GPUs including H100/V100-like systems with dynamic queues and KV-cache utilization; serving stack and interconnect are unspecified.
limits: The description omits workload traces, GPU configurations, predictor error, SLO targets, and baseline tuning.
Latency and SLO gains may depend on request mix, queue regime, and model-placement policy.
Official description only; serving quality and overhead require paper-level verification.

title: UniNL: Unifying Fragmented Non-Linear Operators for Efficient Edge LLM Inference
evidence_span: UniNL decomposes nonlinear LLM operators into primitive pointwise operations, approximates them polynomially for PE-array execution, adds lightweight accelerator extensions, and fuses primitives behind matrix operations; the official description reports 6.89x speedup and 7.26x energy-efficiency improvement over Jetson AGX Orin, plus 1.46x/1.35x performance over state-of-the-art designs.
problem: Edge LLM accelerators underutilize processing elements during fragmented nonlinear operators because matrix-centric designs lack general fusion mechanisms.
method_or_artifact: Primitive decomposition, polynomial approximation, microarchitectural support, and primitive-aware fusion overlapping nonlinear and matrix execution.
workload_or_benchmark: Edge LLM inference with nonlinear operators; model suite, sequence lengths, accuracy impact, and competing design configurations are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Custom accelerator with PE array and lightweight nonlinear-operation extensions; Jetson AGX Orin baseline, process, precision, memory hierarchy, and power measurement boundary are unspecified.
limits: The description omits models, precision, accuracy, accelerator area, clock, memory traffic, and energy boundary.
Polynomial approximation and fusion may trade off accuracy and hardware complexity.
Official description only; performance and quality claims require paper-level verification.

title: Differentiable Fill Insertion with Explicit Delay Optimization
evidence_span: DiffFill jointly optimizes fill uniformity and signal delay by using a Transformer-based CapFormer capacitance extractor and a differentiable Elmore-delay objective; the official description says it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art fill-insertion methods without numeric results.
problem: Traditional fill insertion optimizes density and proxy objectives while remaining misaligned with actual signal delay.
method_or_artifact: Differentiable fill-insertion framework with learned capacitance extraction and explicit Elmore-delay optimization.
workload_or_benchmark: Physical-design fill insertion; layouts, process node, density constraints, delay paths, and comparison metrics are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Interconnect capacitance and delay modeled for semiconductor physical design; extraction tool, layer stack, routing rules, and signoff conditions are unspecified.
metrics: Significant improvement over state of the art claimed qualitatively
limits: No delay, density, capacitance, runtime, or design-quality values are supplied.
Learned capacitance accuracy and Elmore approximation may not match signoff extraction across nodes.
Official description only; physical-design validity requires paper-level verification.
